To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy division multiple-access protocol can be used to achieve higher throughput in wireless networks.
the proposed protocol achieves higher efficiency than the classical protocols in the case of large number of users and small signal-to-interference ratio.

the proposed protocol is a promising solution for multiuser communication, and that its efficiency can be increased when jointly applied with other protocols, such as time division multiple access (TDMA), frequency division multiple access (FDMA) and code division multiple access (CDMA).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a novel multiple-access protocol for energy-limited wireless devices, which can be used to improve the efficiency of existing multiple-access techniques, especially in sensor networks and personal-area networks.
the development of novel multiple access techniques that can be implemented in low-power, short range wireless communication systems.
the design and analysis of multi-user communications based on energy division.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy-based scheme is an attractive option for multiple access in the context of sensor networks, especially when the same low-cost terminal is deployed in large numbers.
the proposed scheme is an efficient alternative to classical multiple-access protocols.
the proposed scheme, in conjunction with classical protocols, can be a good candidate for the future wireless networks, especially in sensor networks and personal-area networks.

, the energy division multiple access (EDMA) scheme is a simple and effective method to improve the performance of a wireless system, and it is especially useful in the case where the number of users is large.
the proposed energy-based protocol is capable to provide higher throughput and better fairness than the conventional time-division multiple access and frequency-division multiple access schemes.

the proposed scheme can provide a good tradeoff between the number of users and the required energy for decoding.
